title: Restraint
note: This is holding body, speech and mind back from evil paths. It follows impartiality because it belongs to someone who sees their own faults as they see a stranger’s.

couplets.plain: Restraint will carry you among the immortals. Lack of restraint will drive you into deep darkness.
couplets.pm: The righteousness of restraint later carries you to the world of the gods. The sin of lacking it drives you into a darkness hard to endure. That darkness is one particular hell.

links.quote: Restraint will carry you among the immortals
links.reason: Sets the immortals against deep darkness as the two ends of the road.
Lack of restraint ends in a dark that is hard to bear.

couplets.plain: Guard restraint as wealth. There is no greater gain for a life.
couplets.pm: No wealth for living beings is greater than restraint, so take it as your true treasure and guard it from loss. “Living beings” here means human life, since only humans know restraint and benefit from it.

links.quote: no greater gain for a life

couplets.plain: If you know what is worth knowing and hold yourself in by the right way, your restraint will be noticed and bring you honour.
couplets.pm: If you understand that restraint is your true knowledge and hold yourself in by the right path, the good will recognise that restraint and it will bring you distinction. For a householder the path of restraint is to keep body, speech and mind under his own control.

links.quote: hold yourself in by the right way
links.reason: Says that restraint, rightly practised, is noticed and brings honour.

couplets.plain: One who holds steady in their place and keeps restraint stands taller than a mountain.
couplets.pm: The stature of one who stays on his path of home life and keeps restraint is far greater than the height of a mountain. This is restraint kept while still enjoying the objects of the senses.

links.quote: holds steady in their place and keeps restraint
links.reason: Gives one who stays in their place and keeps restraint a stature past a mountain’s.

couplets.plain: Humility is good in everyone, but in the rich it is a further wealth.
couplets.pm: Restraint without pride is good in everyone alike, but among them only the rich gain from it a distinction that is another wealth. Those with learning and good birth are held in by these very things, so their restraint doesn’t stand out. These five couplets tell the excellence of restraint in general.

links.reason: Finds it good in everyone, and a further wealth in the rich.

links.quote: in the rich it is a further wealth
links.reason: Tells the person riding high that humility is a further wealth.

couplets.plain: If in one life you can draw in the five senses as a tortoise draws in its limbs, it will shelter you through seven lives.
couplets.pm: If in one birth you can hold in the five senses as a tortoise holds in its five limbs against danger, that power shields you in all seven births. As it keeps out danger, you must keep out sin. The fruit of deeds done in one birth follows you for seven. This tells restraint of the body.

links.remove: ஏமாப்பு is shelter, not treasure. The image of savings isn’t in the Tamil.

couplets.plain: Whatever else you fail to guard, guard your tongue. If you don’t, you will suffer from the slips of your speech.
couplets.pm: Even if you can’t guard all you should guard, guard the tongue alone. Those who don’t guard it fall into the faults of speech and suffer for it themselves.

couplets.plain: If a single evil word does its harm, the good you have done turns bad.
couplets.pm: If even one hurt comes to others through the meaning of your evil words, the good that your other righteous acts brought you turns bad. Evil words are harmful lies, slander and harsh speech. Some read it as one evil word among many good ones.

links.quote: the good you have done turns bad
links.reason: One evil word is enough to turn all one’s good to bad.

links.quote: If a single evil word does its harm

couplets.plain: A wound burned by fire heals within. A scar burned by the tongue never heals.
couplets.pm: A wound someone burns on you with fire stays on the body but heals at once in the mind. The scar burned by a tongue of hot words never heals, even there. So one is called a wound and the other a scar. Both burn, but hot words are crueller than fire. These three couplets tell restraint of speech.

links.quote: A wound burned by fire heals within
A scar burned by the tongue

couplets.plain: Righteousness finds the path to someone who holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint, and waits for the moment to see them.
couplets.pm: The god of righteousness goes down the path to one who keeps anger from rising, is learned and can hold back, and watches for the right moment. Holding back is the mind staying in righteousness and not spreading outward. The right moment is when he is pleasant in mind, speech and face. Righteousness itself comes to such a person. This tells restraint of the mind.

links.quote: holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint
links.reason: Has righteousness find the path and wait for a moment with one who keeps restraint.
